summary: GADR is a LangGraph multi-node workflow (extraction, critique, refinement, RAG over an OSS ADR corpus plus Tavily web search, formatting) using Gemini 3.1 Pro to turn noisy meeting transcripts into Nygard-format ADR drafts. A feasibility study covers five transcripts (four undergraduate teams, one senior-researcher health R&D team), qualitative comparison with zero-/few-shot prompting over 3 rounds, 15 student respondents, and four senior reviewers.

claims.claim: The agentic workflow captures most expert-identified decisions.
claims.evidence: §5.3: seniors listed 23 reference decisions; agent produced 17 ADRs covering 'approximately 18' of them under a decision-level mapping. Mapping procedure and inter-rater agreement not reported; authors note the expert baseline itself was incomplete for Groups 4 and 5.

claims.claim: Agentic workflow is more stable and structurally adherent than zero-/few-shot prompting.
claims.evidence: §5.1: 5 transcripts x 3 rounds; comparison is described qualitatively (variance in ADR count, formatting) with an excerpt figure (Fig. 2) but no counts or variance numbers are tabulated.

claims.claim: Participants found the ADRs clear, complete and useful for recall.
claims.evidence: §5.2: 15 respondents, 55 decision-level evaluations: 52/55 agreed with extracted decision, 51/55 clear and complete, 51/55 helped recall, 49/55 aided learning. Students rated their own projects (familiarity bias acknowledged in §7).
§5.1 and §5.3: concrete traced examples ('500 concurrent connections and 5000+ DAU' from an unrelated retrieved ADR; '93% industry adoption'); tentative discussions promoted to accepted decisions.

patterns.note: Role-separated graph nodes (extract/critique/refine/format) vs single prompt; only qualitative evidence of benefit.
RAG over external ADR corpus enriches drafts but injects unsupported facts from unrelated projects.
Findings consistently argue outputs must remain human-reviewed drafts; failure modes observed directly.
Shared mutable LangGraph state makes steps auditable; traceability used to locate the hallucinated fragment.
Internal critique node acts as an LLM self-reviewer; not separately evaluated.

methodology.sample: 5 meeting transcripts (4 student teams of 4-7, 1 team of 4 senior researchers); 15 student respondents / 55 evaluations; 4 senior reviewers / 23 reference decisions.
methodology.baselines: Zero-shot and few-shot prompting with the same model (reasonable but simple; no other ADR generators compared).
methodology.variance: 3 rounds per approach, but no quantitative variance reported.
methodology.ablations: None (e.g., no critique-node or RAG-off ablation despite RAG being the main source of hallucination).
methodology.languages: Natural-language transcripts (language not stated in excerpts read; Brazilian context).

standards.peer_review: 40th Brazilian Symposium on Software Engineering (SBES 2026) per front matter; not in arXiv comment field.
standards.preregistration: None; ethics committee approval and informed consent stated.

biases.detail: Students evaluated ADRs from their own projects (familiarity bias), mostly undergraduate setting.
Decision-level mapping of agent ADRs to expert decisions appears to be done by the authors without reported agreement statistics.
Stability claim vs baselines is qualitative despite 3 rounds.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None (Gemini used as backbone, not evaluated as a product).

verdict_reason: Honest, self-described feasibility probe with released artifacts and concrete failure analysis, but tiny sample, qualitative baseline comparison, single model, and familiarity-biased participant ratings.
applicability: Tangential to the Java services harness, with one useful lesson. If the team uses agents to draft ADRs or specs from design meetings while rolling out spec-driven development, keep the drafts in a human-review queue. Ground retrieval in the team's own past ADRs, not external corpora, and require a source link for each claim, because retrieval from unrelated projects inserted invented numbers and agents promoted tentative ideas to accepted decisions. The one health-domain transcript (Gov.br authentication, RNDS integration) involved senior researchers, but there are too few samples to draw conclusions for the domain. The paper says nothing about multi-repo work or mixed agent hosts.
